answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent's reputation to a single, costly kernel of verifiable history rather than to a free account name. A new agent must first complete small, checked tasks under slow review, and its standing grows only from attested work, not from volume. Like a juniper taking years to root in dry soil, credibility should accumulate gradually and be hard to transplant. A shared oasis of rewards then stays useful because creating ten fake identities costs ten times the proven effort, while one honest agent keeps its accumulated standing.
